newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Burton optimistic on growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Burton optimistic on growth.

text.p: British fashion retailer Burton Group Plc said on Thursday it was optimistic it could keep growing, but saw a slower pace of improvement in gross margins.

Finance director Andrew Higginson said: "We've just announced a 23-percent increase in profit before tax which is another increase on a very good year last year so...fingers crossed we seem to be still delivering."

Higginson told Reuters the group had had a good run on boosting gross margins for the last three or four years. "I think there is still some scope for gross margin improvement, but it's probably going to be gentle now as opposed to dramatic."
Gross margins improved by one percentage point in the first half.

Higginson said he expected costs to rise in the second half at the same pace as in the first, when they went up 11 percent overall and by 6.4 percent excluding home shopping. Last year Burton moved into mail order via the purchase of Innovations and Racing Green.

The group is in the process of integrating its new mail order operations. Racing Green will be developed by its Principles fashion chain, Hawkshead catalogue by Burton Menswear and Innovations by Debenhams.

Higginson said there were plans to launch catalogues of Burton brands such as Dorothy Perkins and Evans by the autumn. He was optimistic about prospects for mail order as an extension of the store brands.

"We've got very high charge card useage," he said. "Getting on for 40 percent of our sales are on our own cards - as a consequence we've got a very good up-to-date name and address database." This would allow the group to target customers who already shop at Burton outlets.
Burton has joined a growing list of retailers eager to capitalise on the direct mail market, following the success of retailing rival Next Plc's Directory.
The group also announced it was adding 25 percent more space to its flagship Top Shop store at Oxford Circus in London.

Higginson said the revamp would include cafes and fashion features. U.S. sportswear maker Nike will take 70,000 square feet on the Regent Street side of the site and open the first NikeTown sportswear shop in Europe.
"To put Nike in the same building will mean there will be a huge number of people wanting to go there - so both should feed off each other," he said.
All Burton's retail businesses increased profits in the half year, except Burton Menswear, which saw profits fall to 3.8 million stg from 6.1 million.

Higginson said the menswear market in general was proving much tougher for retailers than womenswear. But the group would continue to try and improve its performance. "We've got the largest menswear brand and we'll build on that," he said.
The company has tested out a new format called "Style Union" which brings more brands into the store and it will probably test out a few more. "We are learning from that," Higginson said.

Earlier Burton reported a 22.7 percent increase in pretax profits to 108.1 million stg. The group's shares were 6.5 pence lower at 147.5 pence by 0850 GMT. The profits were slightly below the top end of market forecasts which were 110 million stg.
